How to find cheap flights

Updated 2026-06-22 · 7 min read · Magellan Flights

Finding cheap flights isn't luck and it isn't a secret “hack” — it's a handful of habits that stack up. Do these nine things and you'll pay less than the person in the next seat almost every time. The biggest one? Knowing what a fare is supposed to cost.

Quick answer

To find cheap flights: book in the sweet spot (1–3 months domestic, 2–8 months international), stay flexible on dates and airports, fly mid-week, use a fare tracker so you recognize a real drop, and act fast when a fare falls below its normal range. Knowing the normal price is the biggest lever.

Open the tracker →

9 tricks that actually work

  1. Book in the sweet spot — 1–3 months ahead for domestic, 2–8 for international. Too early or too late both cost more.
  2. Know the normal price. You can't spot a deal without a baseline. Track a route so you know whether today's fare is genuinely low.
  3. Be flexible on dates. Shifting a day or two — especially to Tuesday, Wednesday, or Saturday — often beats every other trick.
  4. Be flexible on airports. A nearby airport, or a cheap hub plus an onward budget flight, can slash the total.
  5. Fly the cheap season. Off-peak and shoulder months are dramatically cheaper for the same destination.
  6. Set fare alerts. Let the price come to you instead of refreshing searches.
  7. Consider two one-ways. Mixing airlines on a one-way each direction is sometimes cheaper than a single round-trip.
  8. Search anywhere. If you're flexible on where, let the cheapest destination pick itself.
  9. Act fast on real drops. The best fares vanish in hours — when one falls below its normal range, book it.

Want shortcuts? Our live board already does the tracking, the “search anywhere,” and the “below-normal” flag for you.

The one trick that beats the rest

If you only do one thing: know the normal price. Every other tip is noise without a baseline. A “$600 flight to Rome” means nothing until you know that route usually runs $750 — then it's a buy. That's the entire idea behind tracking fares like a market, and it's why a tracker beats endless manual searching. The U.S. Bureau of Transportation Statistics publishes average-fare data if you want to sanity-check a route's ballpark.

What our live data adds

We watch 494 routes from the USA and log every price daily, so the deals you see are already filtered to the ones below their normal range. The current standout is Kelowna, about 54% under its usual fare. If a flight is cancelled or delayed after you book, the DOT's consumer protection office explains what you're owed.

Frequently asked questions

What is the cheapest way to find flights?

Track the route so you know its normal price, stay flexible on dates and airports, and book when a fare drops below normal. A fare tracker beats searching one route repeatedly.

What is the best site to find cheap flights?

Use a tool that shows a route's price history and flags fares below normal, so you can tell a real deal from a random number — that context matters more than the search box itself.

How do I find cheap flights to anywhere?

Search 'anywhere' from your home airport and let the cheapest destination surface, then build a trip around the deal instead of picking the destination first.

Does searching in incognito mode find cheaper flights?

No — that's a myth. Clearing cookies or using incognito doesn't meaningfully lower fares. Timing, flexibility, and knowing the normal price are what actually work.
